content:
A woman dubbed "Mother of the Year" by the San Francisco Giants broadcast team in a viral video has spoken out to defend her husband after the clip prompted internet users to attack him.

The incident occurred last Tuesday, when the couple and their daughter were filmed on the stairs of Oracle Park: the wife holding a baby and several food containers, while the husband nonchalantly started eating, leaving the seemingly aggrieved mother to watch from the side. The footage turned them into a talking point online.

The sports commentary duo of Duane Kuiper and Mike Krukow heaped praise on the woman for multitasking, calling her an "Olympic champion" and "Mother of the Year." The pair cast the husband as a villain who only cared about getting his ketchup and was inconsiderate—a view shared by internet users.

So Erika—who says she prefers not to reveal her surname—decided to mount a forceful rebuttal.

In a Substack post published on September 25, she wrote: "Millions of people have seen me carrying my daughter and our food back to my seat at a San Francisco Giants game." "They crowned me 'Mother of the Year' and hurled every insult imaginable at my husband. Some people sent me direct messages or posted TikTok videos explaining why I should leave him."

She continued: "My name is Erika. Our baby's name is Anastasia. My husband's name is Ramses. Before you judge our marriage, please hear from the woman you claim to be defending."

Erika went on to make an impassioned plea in the post:

"Ramses is an outstanding husband and an even more outstanding father. We have been together for nine years and are raising two children under the age of two. I know exactly how he treats me, how he cares for our kids, and what he does for our family. A conversation the audience couldn't hear became the basis for millions of people making sweeping judgments about our lives."

She added that Ramses had originally offered to hold Anastasia so that Erika could use the restroom (he later decided to go get food instead). He also asked whether she wanted to eat first, and whether she needed him to carry the containers. She declined each time, and he was at the time grieving the loss of a friend.

She wrote: "Our marriage allows either of us to lean on the other when we need to." "That night, I chose to take care of him. The camera captured one moment of me looking after my husband, but it couldn't show the countless times he has done the same for me."
